_comment: Mutation arms whose mutation IS applied and whose named assertion does not see it, with
the reason, the SUBJECT that would see it, and who can produce that subject.
THIS FILE FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, like `ledger.json` beside it and
`ci/test/ci-coverage.known-dark.txt` one directory over. A registered arm that SURVIVES is
reported, counted, and does not fail the run. A registered arm that is KILLED fails the run
by name, demanding the entry be deleted — so an entry cannot outlive the gap it records, and
nobody has to remember to clean up after closing one.
ONLY A SURVIVAL IS EXCUSED. A registered arm that reports NEVER RAN still fails, and that is
the whole difference between this register and an exemption list. An entry says: this
mutation reaches the artefact, the assertion named below is green with the defect in place,
and here is the subject that would make it red. It does not say the arm may be broken — a
`find` that stopped matching, an assertion that was renamed, a tree that did not come back
are all still failures under an entry, because none of them is the claim the entry makes.
AN ENTRY IS ONLY LEGITIMATE WITH ALL SIX FIELDS, and `selftest.mjs` refuses the register
otherwise rather than reading around a missing one:
reason    — what the arm asserts and what is green with the mutation in place
cause     — WHY it survives, from readings and not from inference
subject   — the subject that would kill it, concretely enough to go and build
closed_by — who can produce that subject, and where the work lives
evidence  — what was measured, when, and on what tree
recorded  — the date this entry was written, so the debt is dated and not merely present
NOT LEGITIMATE, and the reason the bar is written down while this file is one entry long:
an arm that survives because the ASSERTION is weak does not belong here — strengthen the
assertion. An arm that survives because its mutated reading was taken from a session that
never came up does not belong here either — that is an instrument that did not run, and it
is reported as a stall, not as a survival. Both of those were live questions on the day this
file was written (`O/the-export-answers-for-the-live-path` was the first, fixed by making
the assertion per-region; `O2/a-control-on-every-row` is the second, still open), and both
were kept OUT of this file on purpose. A register whose bar is set once it is already long
gets the bar its longest-serving entries deserve.
COUNT THE KEYS IN `known_survivors`; do not trust a sentence here saying how many there are.
`ledger.json` records that its own summary line has been wrong four times, which is the one
error a register cannot afford, so this file does not carry that sentence at all.

P4/no-frame-is-current-on-a-live-session.reason: The arm removes `session_view.selectionDetail`'s position fallback — the loop that picks a frame by comparing `f.step` against `v.controls.step` when nothing has been marked `current` — and its named assertion, "LIVE: exactly one frame is current on arrival, before anything is clicked", stays GREEN. The mutation is applied, reaches the hydration bundle, and changes nothing observable on any surface a journey can drive.
P4/no-frame-is-current-on-a-live-session.cause: THREE WRITERS MARK A FRAME BEFORE `selectionDetail` EVER CONSULTS THE FALLBACK, and that was established by three readings rather than argued. (1) `selectCalltraceFrame` writes `CalltraceVM.selectedEntry` on a row click — the arm survived the post-click assertion at `clicked="calculate_damage" panel="calculate_damage"`, because the click writes the selection itself. (2) `selectLandingFrame` writes it on the landing — so the arm survived a newly added ARRIVAL assertion too, which is the reading the fallback would have to be load-bearing for. (3) Behind that, the recovery ANCHOR: re-aiming the mutation at `selectLandingFrame`'s own position walk (`if lines.len == 0: return false` forced true, so the walk never runs) ALSO survived, at "counted 1, the claim says 1", because `selectLandingFrame` tries `s.selectCalltraceFrame(anchor)` first and returns before the walk. With any of the three having marked a frame, `selectionDetail`'s first loop always sets `chosen` and the branch beneath it is unreachable.
P4/no-frame-is-current-on-a-live-session.subject: A LIVE session with NO recovery anchor whose `visibleLines` are empty at seed time. That is the one state in which all three writers decline and `selectionDetail` reaches the fallback: no anchor for `selectLandingFrame` to resolve, nothing for its position walk to walk, and no click yet. The corpus the journeys drive has no such recording — every subject either carries an anchor or seeds visible lines — so the arm's assertion is correct and simply has nothing to be correct ABOUT. Killing this arm needs that subject, not a stronger assertion.
P4/no-frame-is-current-on-a-live-session.closed_by: Whoever adds such a recording to the corpus the journeys drive, in THIS repository — `tools/journeys/lib/corpus.mjs` selects subjects from the served markup, so the work is a published recording that seeds no anchor and no visible lines, plus the subject filter that selects it. Then re-run `node tools/journeys/selftest.mjs --arm P4/` and delete this entry; the run will demand the deletion by name.
P4/no-frame-is-current-on-a-live-session.evidence: Measured 2026-09-28 in worktree `blocktracer-ci-green-env`, branched from `origin/dev`, over `client/dist` built by `just export-hydrated` against the three pinned sibling trees (codetracer af70456c, isonim 03f83497, nim-everywhere b2ce1c6b). CI run 35389764236 on ef24db5, `journeys-bite (5)`: SURVIVED in 65s, the only non-killed arm in that shard, and the arm's `why` records the same verdict from its author's own earlier readings. The 65s is itself part of the evidence — this is a survival from a session that came up, not from one that stalled.
